task: Implement src/time-match.js and src/time-match.test.mjs for the ESL telling-time game, exactly to the frozen spec in SPEC.md sections 3.1 through 3.6. This is pure logic: no DOM, no browser APIs, no dependencies, ES modules.
requirements: Create src/time-match.js exporting exactly: normalizeTranscript(raw), parseUtterance(raw), matchTime(target, transcripts), spokenForm(target), spokenWords(target). Signatures and return shapes are frozen in SPEC.md 3.1 — do not rename, do not add or remove exports.

Implement the normalisation pipeline of SPEC.md 3.3 in the stated order. Speech engines return times as NUMERALS far more often than as words, so '7:15', '715' and '7 15' must all normalise the same as 'seven fifteen', and '7 o'clock' the same as 'seven o'clock'. This is the single most important behaviour in the module.
Implement the tens+units fold of step 5 exactly: only 20/30/40/50 followed by 1..9 folds. 'seven thirty five' -> 7 35. 'ten thirty' must NOT fold and stays 10 30.
Parse the cleaned token list as an ORDERED SEQUENCE, matching the accepted structures in SPEC.md 3.4. Never scan for the right numbers appearing anywhere in the string — order carries the grammar.

Enforce the o'clock rule of SPEC.md 3.5: o'clock is valid only when minutes are zero. 'seven fifteen o'clock' and 'seven o'clock fifteen' must return reason 'bad-grammar', NOT 'wrong-time'. Any number token left over after a structure is consumed is also 'bad-grammar'.
Distinguish 'bad-grammar' (structure invalid) from 'wrong-time' (structure valid, time is not the target). 'seven o'clock' against target 7:15 is 'wrong-time', because the structure itself is fine.

Accept the past/to forms in SPEC.md 3.4 ('half past seven', 'quarter to eight', 'twenty past three') as correct with preferred:false. They are valid English and must not be marked wrong, even though the game does not teach them.

Implement the alternatives policy of SPEC.md 3.2 exactly: transcripts[0] alone decides grammar; later alternatives are consulted only to rescue a 'no-time' or 'empty' result. Getting this wrong silently defeats the o'clock rule.

spokenForm/spokenWords produce the taught model form: minutes 0 -> "It's seven o'clock.", minutes 1-9 -> "It's seven oh five.", otherwise -> "It's seven fifteen." with minutes as English words ('forty-five', 'twenty-five').
Create src/time-match.test.mjs: a plain node assertion table (no test framework, no dependencies) run with `node src/time-match.test.mjs`, exiting non-zero on failure and printing a pass/fail count.

The test table must cover: every row of the accepted-structures table in SPEC.md 3.4; every row of the rejected-structures table in 3.5; numeral-form STT variants ('7:15', '715', '7 15', '7 o'clock') for at least six different targets; filler-prefixed utterances ('uh it's seven fifteen', 'I think it's seven fifteen', 'it is seven fifteen'); AM/PM trailing on whole hours and on non-whole hours; 'seven oh five' and 'seven five' for 7:05; every whole hour 1:00-12:00; and a sweep over the level-4 five-minute times asserting that spokenWords() round-trips back through matchTime() as a match.
Each assertion must state the expected reason, not merely ok true/false, so a wrong-time/bad-grammar mixup fails the suite.
constraints: SPEC.md is frozen. Implement it; do not redesign it. If a genuine ambiguity or contradiction is found, implement the most reasonable reading and note it in the summary rather than inventing a different design.
Do not create index.html, styles, scene data, speech, game loop, or any other module — this work order is the two files named above and nothing else.
No dependencies, no package installs, no build step. ES module syntax only.
No DOM or browser globals: the module must run under plain node.

Comment the WHY of the non-obvious rules (the numeral-form normalisation, the tens+units fold, the alternatives policy, bad-grammar vs wrong-time). Match the commenting style of .ai/reference/ref-match.js — explain reasoning, not mechanics.

Everything you need is inside this project directory. .ai/reference/ holds read-only copies of the Sight Word Factory game for structural and commenting-style reference only - never import from it, never modify it, never ship it. Do not attempt to read anything outside this project root.
notes:
SPEC.md is the single source of truth and was frozen by the design lead before any code existed. Read it fully before writing anything; sections 3.1-3.6 are the whole of this work order.

Three points carry most of the risk and are worth extra care:

1. NUMERAL-FORM STT. Chrome's recogniser returns spoken times as digits far more often than as words. 'seven fifteen' arrives as '7:15', '715' or '7 15'; 'seven o'clock' as '7 o'clock'; 'seven oh five' as '7:05' or '705'. If normalisation does not fold all of these to the same token sequence the game is unplayable in the browser it targets. Test these explicitly rather than only the word forms.

2. ORDERED PARSING, NOT NUMBER-HUNTING. The grammar rules exist precisely so that the right digits appearing somewhere in the transcript is NOT enough. Parse the cleaned tokens as a sequence and consume a structure; any number token left over is bad-grammar. This is what makes 'seven fifteen o'clock' and 'fifteen seven' fail while 'seven fifteen' passes.

3. bad-grammar vs wrong-time is a real distinction with different game consequences (SPEC.md 3.6), so the test assertions must check `reason`, not just `ok`. A suite that only checks ok/false would pass with the grammar rule completely broken.

Routing context: this reached Codex after gemini returned PERMISSION_DENIED twice and agy-gpt returned TOOL_FAILURE, all adapter-level faults unrelated to the task. Nothing was written by them; the tree is clean at commit b3cb3ce.

.ai/reference/ref-match.js is the sibling Sight Word Factory matcher. Use it for commenting style and layered-matching structure only - the time grammar is a different problem and must not be forced into its word-fuzzing shape. In particular do NOT add phonetic folding or edit-distance fuzz here: a one-edit slip between 'fifteen' and 'fifty' is a different time, not a pronunciation variant.
